findings.title: HW trunk meets the header's sweat inlet side-on: last leg runs east, the inlet faces north (90.0 degrees off axis, elbow at the port)

evidence.measured: Header at (90, 298.66) rotation 90: placed inlet port (90.0, 306.0, z 88.0) direction (0,1,0), i.e. the 1 in sweat socket opens NORTH and the tube must arrive heading south. PR-B-HW-TRUNK's last leg is (64, 306, 83.44) -> (90, 306, 88.0), direction (0.985, 0, 0.173): perpendicular (dot with the inlet axis = 0). The trunk's last vertex IS the port, so the 90 degree turn sits at the socket mouth with 0 in of tube to seat in it. mep.equipment_port_service grades air ports only, and mep.water_manifold_ports counts outlets, so nothing reads the inlet direction.
evidence.expected: A straight stub along the inlet axis (a socket takes the tube end-on; Uponor's drawing shows the 1 in sweat end as a swaged tube end, B = 0.987 in), then the elbow: trunk arrives from y > 306 heading south, or the header is turned so its inlet faces the approach.
evidence.method: Python probe: placed_ports(model) for EQ-B-HW-HEADER inlet direction; ResolvedPipeRun PR-B-HW-TRUNK path/z_m last two vertices; SCRATCH M2/p13.py. Uponor submittal PDF p.1 drawing (B, C, D) read at 400 dpi: SCRATCH M2/uponor/crop-1.png.

findings.source: Uponor submittal 'ProPEX (type L) copper branch manifolds' (uponor.com/en-us/getsubmittalpdf/22338): End type 2 Sweat 1 in, drawing B = 0.987 in end cup
findings.proposed_fix: End the trunk with a straight N-S stub of >= 2 in into the socket, e.g. (83,310) -> (90,310) -> (90,306), or turn the header so its inlet faces the approach. The authored westward detour to x=64 (4 in then 26 in back east) may be there to clear something, so re-run mep.run_interference and check BATH1's y=309.75 leg (z 92.5 over the trunk top about 89.6).

findings.title: All eight header branches turn 2.649 in below the outlet tip; Uponor requires a Tube Talon or bend support for any bend within 6 in, and three branches turn again 1.5 in later; none is billed

evidence.measured: Outlet tips at z 86.149 (basement-relative); every branch's vertex 1 is at 83.5, a 2.649 in drop, then 90 degrees to horizontal (resolved fitting_records: FIT-CU-90-0.5 at vertices 1 and 2 for all 8). BATH1, WASH and BATH2 turn again after a 1.5 in leg (vertex 1 -> 2), FILLER 3.5 in, SAUNA 3 in. Maker's minimum PEX radius 6 x OD = 3.75 in (TUBE_BEND_RULES) exceeds the 2.649 in drop, so it can only be an elbow fitting, and the engine matches every 1/2 in PEX turn to a copper B16.22 pattern (library/fittings.py:193, _supply_elbows), never grading a tube leg between two fittings. takeoff.json pipe_fittings: 89 water_hot elbow-90-0.5in; no Tube Talon F7050750 or A5110500/A5150500 anywhere in prices.toml or the plan.
evidence.expected: Uponor submittal p.2: 'Any bend within 6 inches of the ProPEX connection to the manifold requires the use of a Tube Talon (F7050750) or Bend Support (A5110500 and A5150500).' Either 8 bend supports on the BOM or a drop long enough to form the bend outside 6 in; and a leg between two ProPEX elbows that holds both fittings (not 1.5 in centre to centre).
evidence.method: SCRATCH M2/p7.py (branch vertices, fitting_records); takeoff.json pipe_fittings; grep -n 'F7050750\|Tube Talon' houses/catlin/prices.toml (none). Uponor submittal PDF p.2 text.

findings.proposed_fix: Author the 8 branches with a straight vertical leg of >= 6 in below the tip (the lanes sit at 83.5; lower them to <= 80.1 or hang the header higher: its top is 8.3 in under the 96.94 clear height) or add 8 Tube Talons to [hardware]; lengthen the BATH1/WASH/BATH2 first horizontal leg past 3 in.
